title: Which family names belong to a square?
description: A square is tested against the rule of each family of four-sided shapes. It meets the rules of a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite. Keeko doubts that a square can belong to other families.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shape earns a family name by meeting the rule of that family, not by how special it looks. Watch for students who think a shape with its own name belongs to no other family.

source: Give every family name that belongs to a square.
video_script.why: The child sees that a shape belongs to every family whose rule it meets, so a square carries five family names.
video_script.substitution: the book's own definitions of rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, trapezium and kite tested against a square
video_script.anchor: a square tested against the rule of each family from the summary of the book
video_script.wrong_answer: a square belongs to no other family
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a square belongs to no other family because it has its own name, but a family name comes from a rule.
video_script.payoff_line: A square is a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite

final_answer.value: A square is a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite
final_answer.spoken: a square is a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite

hold_back: A square is a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite
never_show: a family name of a square left out
maths_rules: a square has all angles 90, so it is a rectangle
a square has all sides equal, so it is a rhombus
a square has opposite sides parallel, so it is a parallelogram, and with at least one pair of parallel sides it is also a trapezium
a square has neighbouring sides equal in two pairs, so it is a kite
video_script.design: One idea: test the square against each rule and keep every name that fits. One square stays on the board and a name tag is added after each test.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a square in the middle of the board with a blank list beside it

marks.fam: a blank list of family names appears beside the square

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a square.
<bookmark mark='fam'/>Four-sided shapes come in many families, and each family has its own rule.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which family names belong to a square?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the rule of each family written beside its name, from the summary of the book

marks.test: a tick appears when the shape meets the rule

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>A shape belongs to a family when it meets the rule of that family.
<bookmark mark='test'/>We test the square against each rule in turn.

beats.on_screen: Given: a square, with all angles 90° and all sides equal
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a square, with all angles ninety degrees and all sides equal.

beats.on_screen: To find: every family the square belongs to
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to list every family it belongs to.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: all angles are 90°, so it is a rectangle

marks.ang: the four right angles of the square are marked
marks.name: the name rectangle is added to the list

narration: <bookmark mark='ang'/>Step one, all angles of a square are ninety degrees.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A four-sided shape with all angles ninety degrees is a rectangle.
The square is a rectangle.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: all sides are equal, so it is a rhombus

marks.sides: the four equal sides of the square are ticked
marks.name: the name rhombus is added to the list

narration: <bookmark mark='sides'/>Step two, all sides of a square are equal.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A four-sided shape with all sides equal is a rhombus.
The square is a rhombus too.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: opposite sides are parallel, so it is a parallelogram, and so also a trapezium

marks.par: the two pairs of opposite sides are marked parallel
marks.name: the name parallelogram is added to the list
marks.trap: the name trapezium is added to the list

narration: <bookmark mark='par'/>Step three, the opposite sides of a square are parallel.
<bookmark mark='name'/>That makes it a parallelogram.
<bookmark mark='trap'/>A trapezium needs at least one pair of parallel sides, so the square is a trapezium too.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: neighbouring sides are equal in two pairs, so it is a kite

marks.kite: the two pairs of neighbouring sides light up in turn
marks.name: the name kite is added to the list

narration: <bookmark mark='kite'/>Step four, a kite has two pairs of equal neighbouring sides.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A square has all sides equal, so its neighbouring sides are equal in two pairs.
The square is a kite too.

beats.on_screen: Answer: A square is a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite

marks.ans: the list of five names is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A square is a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the square with one name card, then each family rule ticked against the square

marks.doubt: the square holds a single name card
marks.card: the rule of each family is shown, not the look of the shape
marks.fix: a tick appears on every rule the square meets

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a square belongs to no other family, because it has its own name.
<bookmark mark='card'/>But a family name comes from a rule, not from how special a shape looks.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>If the square meets a rule, it earns that name as well.
